key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within 12-48 hours. Acute presentation. LOCATION: Periumbilical and diffuse (not localized to one quadrant). Cramping throughout mid-abdomen. DURATION: WAVES lasting minutes, repeating every 4-5 minutes. Entire episode lasts hours to days. CHARACTER: COLICKY CRAMPING (COMES AND GOES IN WAVES, not constant). Intermittent, wave-like quality. AGGRAVATING: EATING OR DRINKING worsens vomiting and cramping. Any oral intake intensifies symptoms. Movement during cramp worsens discomfort. RELIEVING: Vomiting provides TEMPORARY relief. Nothing to eat/drink reduces new vomiting. Position doesn't significantly help. TIMING: WAVE pattern - cramps every 4-5 minutes. Progressive worsening over time. Becomes more frequent. SEVERITY: 6-9/10 during cramps, less between waves. Moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: BILIOUS (green/yellow) VOMITING progressively more frequent, ABSOLUTE CONSTIPATION (no stool OR GAS >12-24 hours), progressive abdominal DISTENSION. Tinkling bowel sounds. KEY POSITIVES: Wave-like cramps, bilious vomiting, inability to pass flatus, distension, prior surgery. KEY NEGATIVES: Diarrhea rules out complete obstruction. CONSTANT pain with peritoneal signs suggests strangulation (surgical emergency).

includes.patient_friendly: all at once or very quickly

red_flags: Severe constant pain with fever and peritoneal signs - strangulated bowel, call 911
Bloody vomit or stool - ischemic bowel, needs immediate surgery
Severe abdominal distension with tachycardia - complete obstruction with possible perforation
Previous bowel obstruction - higher risk of recurrence and complications
